mainTopic: A בעל קרי: saying ברכות, learning תורה, and how he becomes pure
overview: The amud opens by asking how רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say ברכות when he still requires him to immerse. The גמרא first says he means only thinking them (הרהור), but a ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה says them aloud. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רבי יהודה treats ברכות like הלכות דרך ארץ, which a בעל קרי may learn. This leads to a ברייתא listing many opinions on how much תורה a בעל קרי may learn, from almost nothing to everything. רבי יהודה בן בתירא teaches that words of תורה, like fire, cannot become טמא, and רב נחמן בר יצחק rules that practice follows him. The גמרא then discusses how a בעל קרי becomes pure: either by immersing in ארבעים סאה or by having nine קבין of water poured on him. There is debate over whether to publicize this easing, whether warm water works, and whether nine קבין suffice only for a sick person. The amud ends as רבין begins telling of an incident in אושא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does require טבילה for an ordinary seminal emission
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a challenge from the previous section. It shows that רבי יהודה exempts only special mixed cases from טבילה, but he still requires טבילה for a plain בעל קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Doesn't רבי יהודה agree that] a woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood does not need טבילה, but someone who is only a בעל קרי is required to immerse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a point it began earlier: רבי יהודה agrees that a plain בעל קרי must immerse. So he cannot hold that a בעל קרי is fully permitted to say ברכות out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה exempts the woman because her טבילה for קרי would not help while she is still a נדה. An ordinary בעל קרי has no such issue, so even רבי יהודה requires him to immerse. That creates a problem for the plain reading of רבי יהודה's words in the משנה, 'מברך'.

steps.title: Reinterpreting רבי יהודה: he means thinking, not saying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's word 'מברך' in the משנה really means thinking the ברכות in the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'he recites the blessing.' Say instead 'he thinks it in his heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how it reads רבי יהודה's ruling: he does not say the ברכות aloud, he only thinks them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה still requires טבילה, the גמרא concludes that he cannot permit speaking the ברכות. So 'מברך' is reread as הרהור. According to this reading, he differs from the תנא קמא only about which ברכות may be thought, not about speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: do not say (read the text this way)
thinks it over in his heart without speaking

phrases.english: Do not say 'he recites the blessing,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading the משנה

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה even accept thinking? A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה accepts הרהור at all, and quotes a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר is the one who requires thinking instead of speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה accept thinking at all? Wasn't it taught: A בעל קרי who has no water to immerse in recites קריאת שמע but does not say its ברכות before or after. When he eats bread, he says the ברכה afterward but not the ברכה beforehand. Where he does not say them, he thinks them in his heart and does not say them with his lips. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave and brings a ברייתא to set up the attack. This step presents רבי מאיר's side, and the next step gives רבי יהודה's opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, thinking in the heart is רבי מאיר's solution. That suggests רבי יהודה is the one who disagrees with relying on הרהור. If so, the reading 'רבי יהודה means מהרהר' looks wrong.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the blessings out loud in every case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה says the ברכות are said aloud in both cases. This shows he does not rely on thinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: In either case, he says them with his lips.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the ברייתא and completes the challenge. רבי יהודה rejects the 'think it in your heart' approach and has the ברכות said aloud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה says the ברכות aloud, the earlier reading that he only means הרהור falls apart. The גמרא now needs a new way to explain how רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי speak ברכות even though he requires טבילה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

steps.title: רבי יהודה treats blessings like הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say ברכות aloud because he puts them in the same category as הלכות דרך ארץ, which a בעל קרי may say.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבי יהודה made [the ברכות] like הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: רבי יהודה really does mean the ברכות are said aloud. A בעל קרי is not barred from them because they are like הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a בעל קרי applies to words of תורה, which need great awe. הלכות דרך ארץ, the guidance on proper conduct, was permitted to a בעל קרי, and רבי יהודה puts ברכות in that lighter category. This way he can require טבילה and still permit the ברכות aloud.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who gives the new explanation
he made them, he treated them as
teachings about proper conduct and manners, treated more leniently than other תורה study

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the question away from how the ברכות are said (thinking or speaking) to what kind of words they are, תורה study or something lighter.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Rabbi Yehuda made them [the blessings]
like the laws of proper conduct (Derekh Eretz).

steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה permits the ברכות aloud because they belong to a category that is permitted to a בעל קרי

steps.title: תורה must be learned with awe, as at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that compares learning תורה in every generation to the giving of the תורה at חורב, where there was fear and trembling.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,' and right after it is written, 'The day that you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב.' Just as there it was with dread, fear, quaking, and trembling, so too here it must be with dread, fear, quaking, and trembling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא as background for the previous step. It explains why words of תורה are restricted for a בעל קרי, while lighter matters like הלכות דרך ארץ are not. The ברייתא continues in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים next to each other are linked: teaching תורה to future generations, and standing at חורב. Learning תורה must therefore carry the awe of מתן תורה. Since a בעל קרי is linked with lightheadedness, he is unfit for such awe-filled learning, which is the basis for his restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall make them known
חורב, another name for הר סיני
just as there, so too here (a comparison formula)

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a baraita]:
'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children' (Deut. 4:9),
and it is written after it:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחוֹרֵב״,

with dread, fear, quaking, and trembling,

steps.raayaObject: That learning תורה requires awe, and so it is restricted for a בעל קרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא based on the nearby פסוקים in דברים ד:ט–י

steps.title: The ruling: severely impure people may learn, but a בעל קרי may not
steps.stepSummary: Based on the fear and trembling of הר סיני, the ברייתא rules that זבים, מצורעים, and בועלי נדות may learn all of תורה, but בעלי קריין may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: זבים, מצורעים, and men who were with נדות may read תורה, נביאים, and כתובים, and may learn משנה, גמרא, הלכות, and אגדות. But בעלי קריין are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 6 now gives its practical ruling. People with very severe טומאה may learn תורה, but a בעל קרי may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks backwards, because a בעל קרי's טומאה is lighter than a זב's. The reason comes from the הר סיני comparison: learning needs fear and seriousness. קרי usually comes from lightheadedness, so it clashes with that fear, while the other טומאות come from illness or things outside a person's control.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said: a ruling drawn from what came before
People with a זיבה discharge, a severe טומאה
Men who were with a נדה
Men who had a seminal emission

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a בעל קרי is 'more טמא' than a זב. His טומאה is actually lighter. The ban is about lightheadedness clashing with the fear needed for תורה, not about how severe the טומאה is.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Zavim, lepers, and those who were with menstruating women
are permitted to read Torah, Prophets, and Writings,
and to learn Mishnah, Gemara, halachot, and aggadot.
But those who had a seminal emission are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 6 by drawing the practical ruling from the הר סיני comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That a בעל קרי is banned from learning, which is the background for the question about רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא comparing learning to מעמד הר סיני

steps.title: Three opinions on how much a בעל קרי may learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי allows only familiar learning, רבי יונתן בן יוסף allows deeper משנה study, and רבי נתן בן אבישלום allows even גמרא, as long as he does not say ה׳'s names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: he may review familiar material, as long as he does not explain the משנה in depth. רבי יונתן בן יוסף says: he may explain the משנה, but not the גמרא. רבי נתן בן אבישלום says: he may even explain the גמרא, as long as he does not say the names of ה׳ in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now lists תנאים who disagree about exactly how far the ban on a בעל קרי goes. Each one is a bit more lenient than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows only review of what he already knows. רבי יונתן בן יוסף adds explaining the משנה. רבי נתן בן אבישלום adds even deep גמרא analysis, and keeps only one limit: not saying ה׳'s names.

keyTerms.meaning: Material a person is used to learning, plain review
Spreads out and explains in depth

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He reviews what he is used to learning,
as long as he does not explain the mishnah in depth.
Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says:
He may explain the mishnah in depth,
but he may not explain the Gemara in depth.
Rabbi Natan ben Avishalom says:
He may even explain the Gemara in depth,
as long as he does not say the names of God in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹנֶה הוּא בָּרְגִילִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the general ban from Step 7 by giving several opinions on its limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on a בעל קרי has degrees: from review only, to משנה, to גמרא without ה׳'s names.

steps.title: The strictest view: no מדרש at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, quoting רבי עקיבא, says a בעל קרי may not do מדרש at all. Another version says he may not even enter the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, the student of רבי עקיבא, says in רבי עקיבא's name: he may not go into מדרש at all. Some say: he may not go into the בית המדרש at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the strictest opinion. It comes in two versions: either no מדרש learning at all, or not even entering the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions differ on one word. 'למדרש' means he may not do any interpretive learning. 'לבית המדרש' goes further: he may not even walk into the study hall.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: an alternate version of the teaching

says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.english: He may not enter the study hall at all.

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a בעל קרי may learn הלכות דרך ארץ. This supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in Step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he may learn הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line the גמרא was looking for. רבי יהודה explicitly allows a בעל קרי to learn הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, רב נחמן בר יצחק said רבי יהודה treats ברכות like הלכות דרך ארץ. Here the ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה really does allow הלכות דרך ארץ to a בעל קרי. That explains why he lets him say ברכות out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of proper conduct and manners

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי learn הלכות דרך ארץ, and he puts ברכות in the same category. That is why he allows saying them aloud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He may learn the laws of proper conduct.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹנֶה הוּא בְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ

steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that רבי יהודה allows הלכות דרך ארץ to a בעל קרי

steps.title: רבי יהודה is strict with himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה had a קרי, and his students asked him to teach הלכות דרך ארץ. He went into the river to טבול first, explaining that he is lenient for others but strict for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה once had a קרי and was walking by the river. His students said: Rebbe, teach us a פרק of הלכות דרך ארץ. He went down, immersed, and taught them. They said: Didn't you teach us that one may learn הלכות דרך ארץ? He said: Even though I am lenient for others, I am strict for myself.
steps.whatsHappening: A story shows how רבי יהודה acted himself. He followed his own leniency for others, but went beyond it for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students saw a contradiction, since his own rule allows learning הלכות דרך ארץ without immersing. He explained that the הלכה for everyone is lenient, but he chose extra strictness for himself. His טבילה does not cancel his ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not take his טבילה to mean that the הלכה requires it. He said clearly that others are allowed without it. This was a personal strictness.

His students said to him: Our teacher,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּיקֵל אֲנִי עַל אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: He said to them: Even though I am lenient for others,
I am strict for myself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי יהודה personally acted on the ruling from Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha is lenient for others, but a person may take on strictness for himself.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: דברי תורה do not become טמא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה בן בתירא's principle that words of תורה cannot receive טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה בן בתירא used to say: words of תורה do not become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a much more lenient view. It also sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now every opinion limited a בעל קרי in some way. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the תורה itself cannot be made impure, so a טמא person may learn freely.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle becomes very important in practice. Later the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא regarding learning תורה.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הָיָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira would say:
Words of Torah do not become ritually impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הָיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, lenient view that stands against the restrictive opinions in Steps 7 through 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Words of תורה cannot become טמא, so a טמא person may learn.

steps.title: The stammering student and the verse about fire
steps.stepSummary: A student stammered while learning because he was a בעל קרי. רבי יהודה בן בתירא told him to speak clearly and proved from 'כה דברי כאש' that תורה, like fire, cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A student was mumbling in front of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. He said to him: My son, open your mouth and let your words shine, because words of תורה do not become טמא, as it says: 'Is not My word like fire, says ה׳.' Just as fire does not become טמא, so too words of תורה do not become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A story shows רבי יהודה בן בתירא applying his rule, and he gives a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student mumbled to avoid saying the words of תורה clearly while he was טמא. רבי יהודה בן בתירא used the פסוק comparing ה׳'s word to fire. Fire never takes טומאה, so תורה never does either, and the student may speak openly.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too: a comparison formula

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: תורה is like fire and cannot become טמא, so even a טמא person may learn out loud.

phrases.english: There was an incident with one student

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מְגַמְגֵּם לְמַעְלָה מֵרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא.
phrases.english: who was stammering before Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנִי, פְּתַח פִּיךָ וְיָאִירוּ דְבָרֶיךָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, open your mouth and let your words shine,
for words of Torah do not become impure,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֲלֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם ה׳״,
phrases.english: as it says: "Is not My word like fire, says the Lord",
just as fire does not become impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: so too words of Torah do not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story and a פסוק supporting the principle stated in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That words of תורה do not become טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו כג:כט, 'הלא כה דברי כאש נאם ה׳'

steps.title: The ברייתא's ruling supports רבי אלעאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier ברייתא's line that a בעל קרי may lay out the משנה but not the גמרא. It shows that this supports רבי אלעאי, who said in the name of רב that this is the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: he may lay out the משנה but may not lay out the גמרא. This supports רבי אלעאי, who said in the name of רבי אחא בר יעקב, quoting רב: The הלכה is that he may lay out the משנה but may not lay out the גמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a line from an earlier ברייתא and shows that an אמורא, רבי אלעאי, rules the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a line between two levels of learning. A בעל קרי may go over the plain text of the משנה, but he may not go into the deeper reasoning behind it, called 'גמרא'. רבי אלעאי's ruling in the name of רב matches this exactly, so the ברייתא backs him up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', a formula used to quote back a line from a source already cited
Lays out or goes over the material, explaining it simply
The basic text of the rulings
Here, the reasoning and explanation behind the rulings
'This supports him', a sign that a source backs up someone's view

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גמרא' does NOT mean the Talmud book we are learning. It means the deeper reasoning and analysis behind the משנה. The בעל קרי may go over the basic text but not the in-depth discussion.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: Quoting back a line from the ברייתא brought earlier in the sugya.

phrases.english: he may lay out the Mishnah
phrases.notes: The subject is the בעל קרי.

phrases.english: but may not lay out the Gemara.
phrases.notes: גמרא here means the reasoning behind the rulings.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi El'ai,
for Rabbi El'ai said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov said in the name of our teacher:
The halacha is: he may lay out the Mishnah
but may not lay out the Gemara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רבי יהודה בן בתירא and goes back to a detail from the earlier ברייתא about what a בעל קרי may learn.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעאי's ruling (in the name of רב) that a בעל קרי may lay out the משנה but not the גמרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line 'מציע את המשנה ואינו מציע את הגמרא'

steps.title: The same question is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this ruling is one side of a dispute among תנאים. רבי מאיר holds the משנה is allowed and the גמרא is not. רבי יהודה בן גמליאל, quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, either forbids both or (in another version) permits both.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute among תנאים. He may lay out the משנה but not the גמרא; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: both are forbidden. Some say he said: both are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ruling from the last step is really one opinion in an older argument among תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three positions. רבי מאיר takes the middle path: the משנה is allowed and the גמרא is not. The other תנא's view comes in two versions, either the strictest (nothing allowed) or the most lenient (everything allowed).

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like a dispute of תנאים', meaning this question was already argued over by the תנאים
'This and that', meaning both the משנה and the גמרא
'And some say it this way', introducing another version of the same statement

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of Tannaim:
he may lay out the Mishnah
but may not lay out the Gemara,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel:
both this and that are forbidden.
And some say he said: both this and that are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the ruling of Step 14 inside a wider dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the משנה is permitted and the גמרא is forbidden. The other view: both are forbidden, or in another version, both are permitted.

steps.title: Matching each version to an earlier opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the 'both forbidden' version follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, and the 'both permitted' version follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said both are forbidden holds like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. The one who said both are permitted holds like רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects each version of the תנא's view to opinions we already learned earlier in this sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר said a בעל קרי may not learn at all (Step 9), so he would forbid both the משנה and the גמרא. רבי יהודה בן בתירא said words of תורה cannot become טמא (Steps 12–13), so he would permit both.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The one who said', used to identify which view goes with which opinion
The תנא who held that a בעל קרי may not learn at all
The תנא who held that words of תורה cannot become טמא

phrases.english: The one who said both this and that are forbidden
holds like Rabbi Yochanan the Sandal-maker,
the one who said both this and that are permitted
holds like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two versions from Step 15 by tying them to the opinions in Steps 9 and 12–13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Both forbidden' follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. 'Both permitted' follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.title: Common practice follows three elders
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the accepted practice follows three elders: רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז, רבי יאשיה on כלאים, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא on דברי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The world's practice follows these three elders: רבי אלעאי about ראשית הגז, רבי יאשיה about כלאים, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא about words of תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the practical bottom line, and it settles our question: people follow רבי יהודה בן בתירא on learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, words of תורה cannot become טמא. So in practice a בעל קרי may learn both משנה and גמרא, and the 'both permitted' view wins. The other two elders are mentioned because the same rule of practice applies to them, and the גמרא will now explain each one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The world practices', meaning this is the accepted custom
The first shearing of sheep's wool, given to a כהן
Forbidden mixtures of seeds or plants
Words of תורה, meaning learning תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The practical bottom line: we follow רבי יהודה בן בתירא. Words of תורה cannot become טמא, so a בעל קרי may learn everything, both משנה and גמרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for the whole discussion about a בעל קרי learning תורה. It is why we do not stop someone from learning because of this kind of טומאה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The world's practice follows these three elders:
like Rabbi El'ai regarding the first shearing,
like Rabbi Yoshiya regarding forbidden mixtures,

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
phrases.english: like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira regarding words of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After laying out all the opinions, gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא: words of תורה do not become טמא, so a בעל קרי may learn תורה.

steps.title: Explaining the first elder: רבי אלעאי on the first shearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the three elders. It quotes a ברייתא in which רבי אלעאי says the מצוה of ראשית הגז applies only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי אלעאי regarding ראשית הגז: as a ברייתא teaches, רבי אלעאי says: ראשית הגז applies only in the Land of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining each of the three elders, beginning with רבי אלעאי's view on the first shearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי holds that the מצוה to give the first shearing of wool to a כהן applies only in ארץ ישראל, not outside it. Since practice follows him, people outside ארץ ישראל do not give ראשית הגז.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught in a ברייתא', introducing a source from the תנאים

phrases.english: Like Rabbi El'ai regarding the first shearing:
as it was taught in a baraita, Rabbi El'ai says:
the first shearing does not apply
except in the Land of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first of the three elders named in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעאי: the מצוה of ראשית הגז applies only in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The second elder: רבי יאשיה on mixed planting in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The practice follows רבי יאשיה, who says a person is liable for כלאי הכרם only when he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed together in one throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי יאשיה regarding כלאים, as it is written: 'Do not sow your vineyard with כלאים.' רבי יאשיה says: a person is never liable until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed in one throw of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second of the three elders and explains which ruling of רבי יאשיה became accepted practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה reads the פסוק narrowly. Torah liability for כלאי הכרם requires two kinds of grain plus a grape seed, all sown together in one hand motion. Because practice follows him, this prohibition applies in a more limited way.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures, here planting different seeds together
A single throw or motion of the hand

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Yoshiya regarding diverse kinds,
as it is written: 'Do not sow your vineyard with diverse kinds,'
Rabbi Yoshiya says:
a person is never liable
until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed
in one throw of the hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the three elders, moving from רבי אלעאי to רבי יאשיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah liability for כלאי הכרם requires sowing two grain kinds and a grape seed together in one hand motion.

steps.title: The third elder: words of תורה cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who taught that דברי תורה cannot become impure, so a בעל קרי may learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי יהודה בן בתירא regarding דברי תורה, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says, דברי תורה do not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third elder. His ruling is the one that matters most for our sugya about a בעל קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah words cannot become impure, an impure person who learns does not damage them. So a בעל קרי does not need to immerse before learning. This settles the earlier dispute (steps 15-16) in favor of the lenient 'both permitted' view.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of Torah, meaning Torah learning

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the halachic basis for allowing a בעל קרי to learn Torah without first going to the מקוה.

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira regarding words of Torah,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Words of Torah do not become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three elders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah words cannot become impure, so a בעל קרי may learn.
steps.whatToRemember: The three elders whose rulings became practice: רבי אלעאי (ראשית הגז only in ארץ ישראל), רבי יאשיה (כלאים only with three seeds together), and רבי יהודה בן בתירא (Torah cannot become impure).

steps.title: זעירי reports that a purity practice was abolished
steps.stepSummary: זעירי came from ארץ ישראל and said 'they abolished immersion.' Another version says he said 'they abolished washing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When זעירי came, he said: They abolished immersion. Some say he said: They abolished washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings זעירי's short report about a practice that was dropped. It records two versions of what he said, and the next step will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי summed up the new practice in two words. The two versions differ on which practice was dropped: the טבילה of a בעל קרי, or washing the hands before תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Ze'iri came, he said:
They abolished immersion.
And some say: They abolished washing of the hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the lenient ruling of רבי יהודה בן בתירא played out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A practice was abolished: the טבילה of a בעל קרי according to one version, washing the hands before תפילה according to the other.

steps.title: Explaining the source of each version of זעירי's report
steps.stepSummary: The 'immersion abolished' version follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא. The 'washing abolished' version follows רב חסדא, who cursed someone who goes searching for water at prayer time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says they abolished immersion follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא. The one who says they abolished washing follows רב חסדא, who cursed a person who goes looking for water at the time of prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where each version of זעירי's report comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dropping immersion fits רבי יהודה בן בתירא: Torah cannot become impure, so a בעל קרי has no need to go to the מקוה. Dropping washing fits רב חסדא: he disapproved of someone who goes searching for water at prayer time, which shows that washing was not required at the cost of the prayer.

phrases.english: The one who says they abolished immersion
follows Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.
The one who says they abolished washing
follows that statement of Rav Chisda,
who cursed one who goes searching for water
at the time of prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two versions of זעירי's report given in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each version of זעירי's report rests on a known source: רבי יהודה בן בתירא for immersion, רב חסדא for washing.

steps.title: Nine קבין of poured water purify a בעל קרי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בעל קרי who has nine קבין of water poured over him is pure, even without going to a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: A בעל קרי who had nine קבין of water poured on him is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא giving a lighter option for a בעל קרי: pouring water instead of full immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally purity comes through immersion in a מקוה. This ברייתא says that, for a בעל קרי, pouring nine קבין of water over himself is enough. This is a special easing for this case only.

keyTerms.meaning: Nine קבין, a set measure of water

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean poured water purifies in general. It is a special easing that applies only to a בעל קרי.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who had a seminal emission, on whom they poured
nine kav of water, is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בַּעַל קֶרִי שֶׁנָּתְנוּ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another easing related to a בעל קרי's purification, continuing the theme of steps 21-22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine קבין of poured water are enough to purify a בעל קרי.

steps.title: How the nine-קבין ruling was passed down
steps.stepSummary: נחום איש גם זו whispered the ruling to רבי עקיבא, רבי עקיבא whispered it to בן עזאי, and בן עזאי taught it openly to his students in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחום איש גם זו whispered it to רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא whispered it to בן עזאי. בן עזאי went out and taught it to his students in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how the nine-קבין ruling was handed from teacher to student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the ruling was only whispered. In this version of the story, בן עזאי then taught it in public. The next step shows that אמוראים disagree about this ending: one version says בן עזאי also only whispered it. The reason for whispering is given in step 26, so scholars would not be with their wives constantly, like roosters.

keyTerms.meaning: In the marketplace, meaning in public

phrases.aramaic: נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ לְחָשָׁהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Nachum of Gam Zo whispered it to Rabbi Akiva,
and Rabbi Akiva whispered it to ben Azzai,
and ben Azzai went out
and taught it to his students in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ לְחָשָׁהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the history of the ruling quoted in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nine-קבין ruling was first whispered privately and then taught publicly by בן עזאי.

steps.title: Dispute over whether בן עזאי taught openly or whispered
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל disagree about the end of the story. One says בן עזאי taught the ruling openly; the other says he also whispered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל disagreed about this, רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא. One taught 'he taught it openly,' and one taught 'he whispered it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records a disagreement about the correct wording of the story's ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether בן עזאי made the ruling public or kept it quiet like his teachers. The answer tells us whether the ruling was meant to be widely publicized or shared only privately.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There is a strong easing for a בעל קרי: Torah cannot become impure, immersion or washing was abolished, and nine קבין of poured water purify. There was hesitation, however, about publicizing it.

phrases.english: Two amora'im in the West disagreed about it,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida.
One taught: 'He taught it openly,'
and one taught: 'He whispered it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the last line of the story in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions of how בן עזאי passed on the ruling: openly or in a whisper.

steps.title: Why one version says openly and the other says whispered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each version: openly, to prevent בטול תורה and בטול פריה ורביה; whispered, so that תלמידי חכמים would not be with their wives constantly, like roosters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who taught that בן עזאי taught it openly held that it was because of neglect of תורה and neglect of having children. The one who taught that he whispered it held that it was so that תלמידי חכמים should not be with their wives all the time, like roosters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each of the two אמוראים from the last step tells the story differently. Each version reflects a different concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching the easy ruling openly helps people. Without it, a בעל קרי might stop learning Torah, or avoid his wife so he would not need a מקוה. Whispering it protects scholars: if purification is too easy, they might spend too much time with their wives and too little time learning.

phrases.english: The one who taught "he taught it" openly,
held it was because of neglect of Torah
and because of neglect of having children.
And the one who taught "he whispered it" held it was
so that Torah scholars should not be
constantly with their wives, like roosters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two versions in step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Openly: to prevent בטול תורה and בטול פריה ורביה. Whispered: to prevent scholars from being with their wives too often.

steps.title: Some are lenient, some are strict, and the strict are blessed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי reports both lenient and strict practices about immersion for a בעל קרי, and says that one who is strict on himself is given long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: I heard that some are lenient about it, and I heard that some are strict about it. Anyone who is strict about it on himself has his days and years made long.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי adds a new statement. He says the practice was never settled, but being strict brings a blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not decide the law. He reports that both practices exist. He still praises the person who chooses to immerse even though he may not have to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
I heard that they are lenient about it
and I heard that they are strict about it,
and anyone who is strict about it on himself,
they lengthen his days and years for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמְּקִילִּין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a statement about how to practice the immersion requirement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law is unsettled, and one who is strict on himself merits long life.

steps.title: What is the point of the morning immersers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks what the value is of those who immerse in the morning, which sounds like he dismisses immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is the value of the morning immersers?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי makes a statement that sounds critical of people who go to the מקוה in the morning. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it sounds like he thinks a בעל קרי needs no purification at all. The גמרא will question this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their value / what is their point?
Those who immerse in the morning (after a קרי at night)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the value of the morning immersers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אמורא's statement on the same topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seems to say that morning immersion has no value.

steps.title: But he himself forbids a בעל קרי from learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: how can רבי יהושע בן לוי dismiss immersion when he himself rules that a בעל קרי is forbidden to learn Torah?
steps.simpleTranslation: "What is their value"?! He is the one who said that a בעל קרי is forbidden to engage in words of Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יהושע בן לוי seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a בעל קרי may not learn Torah until he becomes pure, he obviously needs some way to purify himself. So רבי יהושע בן לוי cannot mean that purification is pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But he himself is the one who said
A man who had a seminal emission
Words of Torah, meaning Torah study

phrases.english: "What is their value"?!
But he is the one who said:
A בעל קרי is forbidden in words of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain reading of step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: he requires purity for Torah study, so he cannot dismiss purification.

steps.title: He meant that a full מקוה is not needed, because pouring is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets him: why use ארבעים סאה when nine קבין work, and why immerse when pouring works?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: Why use forty סאה when nine קבין are possible? Why immerse when pouring is possible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what רבי יהושע בן לוי really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not question purification itself. He questioned only the hard method. A smaller amount of water (nine קבין), poured over the body, is enough, as the ברייתא taught in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the minimum size of a מקוה
Nine קבין, a much smaller amount of water

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי is not saying a בעל קרי needs nothing. He still needs purification, just with nine קבין poured on him instead of a full מקוה.

phrases.english: This is what he meant:
What is the point of forty סאה,
when it is possible with nine קבין?
What is the point of immersing,
when it is possible by pouring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 29
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן לוי dismissed purification altogether
steps.terutzMaskana: He dismissed only the full מקוה, since nine קבין poured over the body is enough

steps.title: Requiring a full מקוה was a great fence against sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the requirement of ארבעים סאה served as a great protective fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: They made a great fence with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא explains why the hard requirement of a full מקוה was valuable. The next step brings proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if nine קבין might technically work, the rule of a full מקוה made sinning harder and more embarrassing. That made it a protection against sin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
They made a great fence with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the value of the strict ארבעים סאה requirement after step 30 made it seem unnecessary
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ארבעים סאה requirement is a powerful safeguard against sin.

steps.title: The woman who stopped a sinner by asking about the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a man who asked a woman to sin. She mocked him, asking if he had ארבעים סאה to immerse in, and he immediately backed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: There was a story of a man who asked a woman to sin with him. She said to him: Empty one! Do you have forty סאה to immerse in? He immediately stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story from a ברייתא to prove רבי חנינא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trouble of finding a full מקוה afterward was enough to stop the man from sinning. This shows the strict requirement really worked as a fence.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל קרי may become pure with nine קבין poured on him, yet the full ארבעים סאה מקוה was praised as a great fence against sin. Being strict brings blessing.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
There was a story of one who solicited a woman
to commit a sin.
She said to him: Empty one!
Do you have forty סאה
that you can immerse in?
He immediately backed off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבי חנינא's statement in step 31
steps.raayaObject: The ארבעים סאה requirement functions as a great fence against sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא story of a man deterred from sin by the need for a full מקוה

steps.title: Warm bathhouses might make immersion easier
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks why the חכמים neglect this immersion and suggests using bathhouses if cold is the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to the חכמים: Why do you treat this immersion lightly? If the problem is cold, bathhouses are available.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא urges the חכמים not to set aside immersion. He offers bathhouses as an answer to the difficulty of cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question is a way of pressing them to act, not a request for a legal definition. The suggestion assumes that bathhouse water can serve for this immersion.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to the Sages:

phrases.aramaic: רַבּוֹתַי, מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתֶּם מְזַלְזְלִין בִּטְבִילָה זוֹ:
phrases.english: My teachers, why do you treat this immersion lightly?
If it is because of the cold, it can be done in bathhouses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story showing the deterrent value of immersion, רב הונא urges the חכמים to practice it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cold water need not prevent this immersion if bathhouses can be used.

steps.title: Can immersion work in warm water?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges the bathhouse suggestion: can immersion take place in warm water?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Is there immersion in warm water?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges the practical solution רב הונא just proposed. He questions whether warm water is valid for this immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If warm water does not work, bathhouses do not solve the cold-water problem. The challenge is to the proposed method, not to the underlying requirement of immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: but is it really so?; introduces a challenge

phrases.english: Rav Hisda said to him:
But is immersion valid in warm water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption that made רב הונא’s bathhouse suggestion possible.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא’s suggestion to immerse in bathhouses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bathhouses help only if warm water is acceptable for this immersion.

steps.title: The warm-water objection has support
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells רב חסדא that רב אדא בר אהבה agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב אדא בר אהבה stands with you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא responds by acknowledging that another חכם shares רב חסדא’s position. The text does not give a further argument for his bathhouse suggestion here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This response identifies a real disagreement about warm-water immersion. It does not say that רב הונא has accepted the objection.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sage רב אדא בר אהבה

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה קָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ.
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava holds like you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה קָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב חסדא by locating his objection within a disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Acknowledgment of a differing view, without a full resolution of the legal question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא’s objection might seem to end the bathhouse proposal.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא notes that רב אדא בר אהבה agrees with רב חסדא; the disagreement remains.

steps.title: רבי זירא requests water to be poured over him
steps.stepSummary: Although רבי זירא is sitting in a tub of water, he asks his attendant to pour nine קבין over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא was sitting in a tub of water in the bathhouse. He told his attendant to bring nine קבין and pour them over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to an incident about the nine-קבין method. רבי זירא asks for water to be poured on him even while he is sitting in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His action sets up the next question: why does the water already around him not suffice? The answer will distinguish sitting in water from having water poured.

keyTerms.meaning: nine קבין, a measure of water

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּאַגָּנָא דְמַיָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira was sitting in a tub of water
in the bathhouse,
he said to his attendant:
Go and bring me nine kav
and pour them over me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּאַגָּנָא דְמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the warm-water disagreement to how the nine-קבין method is performed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא seeks nine קבין poured over him rather than relying on the water in his tub.

steps.title: Why is the extra pouring necessary?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks why רבי זירא needs water poured over him when he is already sitting in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to him: Why does my master need all this? You are already sitting in water!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא asks about רבי זירא’s action. He wants to know why the water in the tub is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question treats sitting in water as a possible substitute for pouring. רבי זירא’s reply will explain why the two actions are not interchangeable.

keyTerms.meaning: why does my master need it?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said to him:
Why does my master need all this?
He is already sitting inside the water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבי זירא’s request is necessary.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether sitting in water can take the place of pouring nine קבין.

steps.title: Each water measure has its own method
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that forty סאה work through immersion, while nine קבין work through pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: It is like ארבעים סאה. Just as ארבעים סאה work by immersion and not by pouring, so תשעה קבין work by pouring and not by immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers that the way the water is used matters. Sitting in water cannot replace pouring for the nine-קבין method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty סאה require immersion, not pouring. Nine קבין have the opposite procedure: they must be poured, so the tub does not accomplish what רבי זירא requested.

keyTerms.meaning: ארבעים סאה, the stated immersion measure
so too; introduces the matching rule

phrases.english: He said to him: It is like forty se’a:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, בִּטְבִילָה וְלֹא בִּנְתִינָה —
phrases.english: just as forty se’a work through immersion and not through pouring—

phrases.aramaic: אַף תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין בִּנְתִינָה וְלֹא בִּטְבִילָה.
phrases.english: so too nine kav work through pouring and not through immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why being seated in the tub did not answer רבי זירא’s need.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forty סאה require immersion; nine קבין require pouring.
steps.whatToRemember: For nine קבין, the water must be poured over the person. Sitting in that water is a different action.

steps.title: A jug measured for nine קבין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן prepares a jug that holds nine קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן prepared a jug with a capacity of nine קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical example of the nine-קבין measure. רב נחמן prepares a container of exactly that capacity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A measured jug makes it possible to use the required quantity. The next report will limit the cases in which this method suffices.

phrases.english: Rav Nahman prepared a jug
that held nine kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן תַּקֵּן חַצְבָּא בַּת תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical way to measure the amount just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן prepared a jug holding nine קבין.

steps.title: A limit on the nine-קבין method
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a teaching that limits nine קבין to a sick person whose emission was involuntary; a sick person described as המרגיל requires forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he reported that רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה גלוסטרא said: This was taught only for a sick person who had an involuntary emission. But a sick person who brought about the emission requires ארבעים סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a teaching that narrows when nine קבין suffice. It distinguishes between two kinds of sick person and requires forty סאה for the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion explained how to use nine קבין; this teaching adds a limit on who may rely on them. It does not change the rule that, when nine קבין are used, they must be poured.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught it only in the case of
a sick person whose emission was involuntary
a sick person who brought about the emission

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה גְּלוֹסְטְרָא אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: he said: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehuda Gelostera said:
They taught this only for a sick person whose emission was involuntary.
But for a sick person who brought about the emission, forty se’a are required.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה גְּלוֹסְטְרָא אָמְרוּ:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the apparent availability of the nine-קבין method illustrated by רב נחמן’s jug.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under this reported teaching, nine קבין suffice for a חולה לאונסו, but a חולה המרגיל requires forty סאה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate questions: how nine קבין must be applied, and which cases may use them.

steps.title: The jug has lost its purpose
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that, under the narrow rule just reported, רב נחמן’s nine-קבין jug is effectively broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב נחמן’s jug is broken.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reacts to the previous rule by saying that רב נחמן’s jug is now of little use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous rule allowed nine קבין only for a sick person whose emission was involuntary. רב יוסף calls the jug “broken” because its use has become very limited, not because it physically broke.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who prepared the jug

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rav Naḥman’s jug is broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִתְּבַר חַצְבֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical consequence from רב דימי’s restriction in step 40.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the restricted rule, רב נחמן’s nine-קבין jug has little use.

steps.title: רבין introduces an incident in אושא
steps.stepSummary: רבין begins a report about an incident in אושא; the incident itself has not yet been told.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: There was an incident in אושא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts to a report from רבין. This line only sets up the incident that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not yet know what happened in אושא or what it will show about nine קבין. The report may affect the discussion, but this line alone gives no new ruling.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said
There was an incident in Usha

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אֲמַר בְּאוּשָׁא הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב יוסף’s reaction to the beginning of a new report.
